# BlockForest survival prediction

```{r}
library(blockForest)
```

# 1. Example data 

```{r}
# NOTE: There is no association between covariates and response for the
# simulated data below.
# Moreover, the input parameters of blockfor() are highly unrealistic
# (e.g., nsets = 10 is specified much too small).
# The purpose of the shown examples is merely to illustrate the
# application of predict.blockForest().


# Generate data:
################

set.seed(1234)

# Covariate matrix:
X <- cbind(matrix(nrow=40, ncol=5, data=abs(rnorm(40*5))), 
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=30, data=abs(rnorm(40*30, mean=1, sd=2))),
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=100, data=abs(rnorm(40*100, mean=2, sd=3))))
colnames(X) <- paste("X", 1:ncol(X), sep="")

# Block variable (list):
block <- rep(1:3, times=c(5, 30, 100))
block <- lapply(1:3, function(x) which(block==x))

# Survival outcome:
ysurv <- cbind(abs(rnorm(40)), sample(c(0,1), size=40, replace=TRUE))

# Divide in training and test data:
Xtrain <- X[1:30,]
Xtest <- X[31:40,]

ysurvtrain <- ysurv[1:30,]
ysurvtest <- ysurv[31:40,]
```


## Perform BlockForest

### Simple

```{r}
# Train the blockForest model
    blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, 
                            blocks = block, nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, 
                            splitrule = "extratrees", block.method = "BlockForest",
                            importance = "impurity")
    
    # Make predictions on the test data
    predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest)
```

### 5fold CV (Outer)

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(blockForest)
library(survival)

# Create a function for cross-validation
cross_validate_blockforest <- function(X, ysurv, folds) {
  results <- vector("list", length(folds))
  
  for (i in seq_along(folds)) {
    # Split the data into training and test sets
    test_indices <- folds[[i]]
    train_indices <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(X)), test_indices)
    
    Xtrain <- X[train_indices, ]
    Xtest <- X[test_indices, ]
    
    ysurvtrain <- ysurv[train_indices, ]
    ysurvtest <- ysurv[test_indices, ]
    
    # Train the blockForest model
    blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, 
                            blocks = block, nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, 
                            splitrule = "extratrees", block.method = "BlockForest",
                            importance = "impurity")
    
    # Make predictions on the test data
    predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest)
    
    # Store the results for evaluation, e.g., store predicted survival functions
    results[[i]] <- list(predictions = predres, 
                         actual = ysurvtest, 
                         variable_importance = blockforobj$forest$variable.importance)
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Create 5 folds for cross-validation
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
n <- nrow(X)
folds <- split(sample(1:n), rep(1:5, length.out = n))

# Run cross-validation
cv_results <- cross_validate_blockforest(X, ysurv, folds)
```

## Performance metrics 

### Integrated Brier Score 

```{r}
library(SurvMetrics)

# Define time of interest
## Option 1: Use times of actual events in test data
IBSrange <- sort(ysurvtest[,1][ysurvtest[,2] == 1])

## Option 2: Generate 100 uniformly spaced points within the time range (min, 0.9 quantile) of the test data
IBSrange <- seq(min(ysurvtest[,1]), quantile(ysurvtest[,1], 0.9), length.out = 100)

SurvMetrics::IBS(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]), predres$survival, IBSrange = c(IBSrange))
```

```{r}
ibs_scores <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  IBS(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]), res$predictions$survival)
})

ibs_scores_1 <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  IBS(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]), res$predictions$survival)
})

# Compare two models
out <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, ibs_scores = ibs_scores, model = "test")
out_1 <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, ibs_scores = ibs_scores_1, model = "test_1")

plot <- rbind(out, out_1)

ggplot(plot, aes(x = model, y = ibs_scores, fill = model))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA)+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,0.3))+
  theme_classic()+
  stat_compare_means()
```

### Concordance (Uno)

```{r}
# timewt specifies 
concordance_scores <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  out <- concordance(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]) ~ rowSums(res$predictions$chf), timewt = "n/G2")
  return(out$concordance)
})

concordance_scores_1 <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  out <- concordance(Surv(res$actual[, 1], res$actual[, 2]) ~ rowSums(res$predictions$chf), timewt = "n/G2")
  return(out$concordance)
})

# Compare two models
out <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, concordance_scores = concordance_scores, model = "test")
out_1 <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, concordance_scores = concordance_scores_1, model = "test_1")

plot <- rbind(out, out_1)

ggplot(plot, aes(x = model, y = concordance_scores, fill = model))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA)+
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,0.3))+
  theme_classic()+
  stat_compare_means()
```


### Kaplan-Meier and risk group definition

```{r}
library(survival)
# Create risk groups based on cumulative hazard estimates
risk_group <- ifelse(rowSums(predres$chf) > median(rowSums(predres$chf)), "high", "low")

surv_test <- survdiff(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ risk_group)
surv_test
```

```{r}
out_df <- as.data.frame(ysurvtest) %>% rownames_to_column("sample") %>% mutate(risk_group_pred = risk_group)

#Plot specific survival curves
fit <- survfit(Surv(out_df$V1, out_df$V2) ~ risk_group_pred, data = out_df)
print(fit)

ggsurvplot(fit,
          pval = TRUE,
          risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
          risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
          linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)

```

### Importance

#### Feature-level

```{r}
# Train the blockForest model with importance measure
blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, blocks = block,
                        nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule = "extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest", importance = "permutation")

variable_importance <- blockforobj$forest$variable.importance

# Calculate block-wise aggregated importance
aggregate_importance <- sapply(block, function(indices) {
  mean(variable_importance[indices])  # Mean importance of variables in each block
})
names(aggregate_importance) <- paste("Block", 1:length(block), sep="_")
aggregate_importance
```


```{r}
variable_importance <- sapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  res$variable_importance
})



plot %in% block

plot <- variable_importance %>% rownames_to_column("feature") %>% pivot_longer(cols = 2:ncol(.),names_to = "fold", values_to = "importance")

ggplot(plot, aes(x = reorder(feature, -importance), y = importance))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_classic()
```

#### Block-level 

```{r}
variable_importance <- lapply(cv_results, function(res) {
  res$variable_importance
})



block_importance #calculate the mean importance values (here impurity)


# Calculate block-wise aggregated importance
aggregate_importance <- sapply(block, function(indices) {
  mean(variable_importance[indices])  # Mean importance of variables in each block
})
names(aggregate_importance) <- paste("Block", 1:length(block), sep="_")
aggregate_importance

block
```

# 1. Clinical-only

## Load clinical data

```{r}
metadata_general <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas_full/projects/RCC_DL/metadata_general.csv")
```


```{r}
colnames(metadata_general)

metadata_select <- metadata_general %>% select(PID, OS_months, status_OS, pT_combined, ISUP_combined, necrose) %>% filter(complete.cases(.))

metadata_select$pT_combined <- factor(metadata_select$pT_combined, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$pT_combined)))

metadata_select$ISUP_combined <- factor(metadata_select$ISUP_combined, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$ISUP_combined)))

metadata_select$necrose <- factor(metadata_select$necrose, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$necrose)))

metadata_select$gender <- factor(metadata_select$gender, levels = sort(unique(metadata_select$gender)))
```


```{r}
set.seed(22)

# Create train/test splits considering similar censoring rates
folds <- createDataPartition(metadata_select$status_OS, p = 0.75, times = 5)

meta_survival <- metadata_select %>% column_to_rownames("PID") %>% select(OS_months, status_OS)
meta_info <- metadata_select %>% column_to_rownames("PID") %>% select(-OS_months, -status_OS)

colnames(meta_info) <- paste0("CLIN_", colnames(meta_info))

x_train <- meta_info[folds[[2]],]
x_test <- meta_info[-folds[[2]],]

y_train <- meta_survival[folds[[2]],]
y_test <- meta_survival[-folds[[2]],]

all.equal(rownames(x_train), rownames(y_train))
all.equal(rownames(x_test), rownames(y_test))
```


```{r}
block <- list()
block[[1]]<- c(1:3)
block
```


## Perform BlockForest

### Simple

```{r}
set.seed(22)
# Train the blockForest model
blockforobj <- blockfor(x_train, as.matrix(y_train), 
                        blocks = block, 
                        splitrule = "extratrees", block.method = "BlockForest",
                        importance = "impurity")
    
# Make predictions on the test data
predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = x_test)
```
